sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Wedemark, a municipality of villages north of Hannover with the S-Bahn stations Bennemühlen, Mellendorf and Bissendorf, has little parking policy that we could find: no official source on paid on-street parking, parking-disc zones or resident parking, no parking-space statute and no council decision on parking. What it has is a transport story. S-Bahn services run from the three stations to Hannover every 30 minutes, and the on-demand 'sprinti' buses have supplemented local transport since June 2021 [7]. By June 2025 sprinti had logged more than 236,000 trips in Wedemark since May 2024, the highest use per head of any municipality in the Region Hannover, with on average 4,400 people boarding a day, and it is included in the normal transit fare [10]. The S4 line suffered a complete outage in January 2026, after which the operator bought in services from an external rail company, and the mayor called for a serious discussion about how S-Bahn operation is organised, including a separate division within üstra [4]. In 2017 the Verwaltungsausschuss awarded a contract for a comprehensive traffic concept, and the notice does not say what came of it [14]. The Region Hannover is preparing a Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan, with a second expert workshop announced for 28 October 2026 in Bissendorf [3], and ran an online participation for its new local transport plan until 15 January 2025 [12].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The recent projects are about the stations. On 15 September 2026 the Region and the mayor opened covered, partly lockable bike-and-ride facilities at Bissendorf and Bennemühlen with 158 bicycle spaces, for about 550,000 euros, of which the state paid about 40 percent [2]. A municipal notice of April 2026 announced that on 27 and 28 April the floor sensors in part of the Bennemühlen P+R would be replaced, and does not confirm completion [1]. On charging, enercity opened the first of 14 public charging points at the town hall in Mellendorf in June 2023, at seven sites [5], and the municipal project MoEWe has covered charging infrastructure and alternative mobility since September 2020 [6]. The first parklet in Wedemark opened in Mellendorf in April 2023 [13], and the stadtmobil car-sharing car at the town hall was announced as bookable all day in summer 2025 [11].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The park-and-ride sites are Deutsche Bahn's: the Bennemühlen P+R has 182 spaces, open round the clock, and the Bissendorf one 67 [0][9]. Hannover.de says all park-and-ride facilities in the GVH area are free to use, but neither it nor the üstra page names these two sites, so their being free is an inference [8].

Our data cover the P+R Bennemühlen, whose feed gives 158 spaces against DB's 182, so the percentages are approximate. Over about 27 days since late September 2026 occupancy averaged about 29% on weekdays and 17% at weekends, with a peak of 77% around midday on a Thursday, which fits a commuter car park. The Bissendorf site and the village centres are not in our data.
